input: # requireValue:false means "a source with no value resolves to the grammar's
# declared emptyResult", and that has to hold for EVERY no-value source, not
# only the exactly-empty one. TypeScript short-circuited on `` alone and let
# whitespace/comment-only sources fall out of the rules as undefined, while Go
# answered nil for all of them. These rows pin the whole set in both runtimes.
# Not a no-value source: a string whose CONTENTS look like a comment. The
# scan stops on the leading quote and never looks inside.
# An unterminated block comment holds no value either, but the engine's own
# unterminated_comment is the better diagnosis and must not be swallowed.
